title: 1. Quick Start

children.title: Window Applications (App)
children.content: Floating desktop-style windows containing your widget. Launched via Applications Grid or Dock. Configurable via width/height boundaries.

children.title: Dashboard Widgets
children.content: Embedded directly onto your main startpage wallpaper. Can be unlocked and dragged freely when rearrange mode is enabled.

children.title: Vertical / Horizontal Panel Shortcuts
children.content: Adds shortcut launcher icons inside the sidebar panel or top header bar. Clicking these launches the sandboxed widget flyout dynamically.

title: 3. HTML Guidelines
content:
Your HTML should contain the main structure of your widget inside a wrapping element. Use semantic HTML where appropriate (e.g. <nav>, <section>). Ensure all elements that require scripting hooks have descriptive, unique IDs.

Note: You do not need to include outer boilerplates like <html> or <body> tags. Write only the inner HTML content that resides inside your widget container.

title: 4. CSS & Transparency Guidelines
5. Theme Styling (.widget.light & .widget.dark)
6. JavaScript Runtime
content: Write standard JavaScript to bind interactions, fetch APIs, or manage widget states. Your code is executed dynamically inside a safe execution scope after the DOM is ready.

title: 7. Widget API
content:
The widget runtime exposes a global widget object to interact with the parent window wrapper:
  • widget.resize(width, height): Dynamically resize your widget window container at runtime. Capped between 100px and the viewport size.
  • widget.close(): Closes the widget application window wrapper.
  • widget.minimize(): Minimizes the widget window container.
  • widget.theme: Returns the active theme string ('dark' | 'light').
  • widget.accentColor.get(): Returns the resolved hex color string (e.g. '#3b82f6') representing the current startpage accent color configuration.

title: 8. Media & Audio Playback API (widget.media)
9. Widget Lifecycle
content:
Understanding the execution sequence helps you structure initialization correctly:
  1. HTML Injected: The layout templates are injected into the DOM tree.
  2. CSS Loaded: Modular styles and reset variables are parsed.
  3. Environment Variables Injected: The ENV object is initialized.
  4. JavaScript Executed: Sandboxed scripts run, binding event hooks.
  5. Widget Interactive: Ready for user interactions.

title: 10. Supported Web APIs
content:
Use native web features directly inside your JavaScript code:
  • ✓ fetch() (for API requests)
  • ✓ WebSocket (for live updates)
  • ✓ URL & URLSearchParams
  • ✓ localStorage & sessionStorage
  • ✓ IndexedDB
  • ✓ Clipboard API
  • ✓ HTML5 Canvas
  • ✓ Web Audio API

title: 11. Environment Variables (.env)
12. Sandbox Limitations
content:
To protect the user's browser, the following security constraints are enforced:
  • No chrome.* APIs: Access to extensions APIs is disabled.
  • No parent window access: Accessing parent frames throws security exceptions.
  • No eval() / dynamic scripts: Dynamic injection is blocked.
  • No filesystem access: Direct file writes are disallowed.

title: 13. Example Widgets
content:
Draw inspiration from these popular widget implementations:
  • GitHub Profile Viewer: Fetches public repositories using API keys.
  • Weather Widget: Renders hourly mock forecasts and icons.
  • Pomodoro Timer: Uses requestAnimationFrame and sound effects.
  • Todo List: Saves tasks locally using localStorage.
  • Music Controller: Manages YouTube/Spotify tabs via widget.media.
